title: Moving the target from 1:1 to 1:3 on the same 1,057 opening range trades cost me 7 points of win rate and flipped it from losing to profitable
author: person-person12
selftext:
QQQ, 5 minute candles, Jan 2020 through Dec 2025. Long only, one trade a day, no filters. The opening range is the first 15 minutes. Entry is the first candle that closes back above the range high, the stop sits 2x ATR below that high, flat by 3:55. The only thing I changed between the three runs was where the target sits.

**1:1** 1,058 trades, 54.5% wins, profit factor 0.99, **-2.3%** net

**1:2** 1,057 trades, 48.3% wins, profit factor 1.03, **+7.0%** net

**1:3** 1,056 trades, 47.7% wins, profit factor 1.04, **+10.0%** net

I expected the win rate to fall off a cliff when I tripled the distance to the target, and it only dropped **6.8 points**, which tells me a lot of the trades hitting the 1:1 target were going to keep running anyway.

The 1:1 version was up **14.9% before costs** and finished at -2.3% after them. Commission and slippage came to about **$17,500** on a 100k account over the six years, charged on both sides of every trade, and thats more than the whole spread between the worst target and the best one. I run these in [Agenticks](https://www.agenticks.ca/?utm_source=reddit&utm_medium=post&utm_campaign=autopilot&utm_content=ai_trading) with real costs charged by default, otherwise all three of these look like winners.

Drawdown barely moved either, 22.2% at 1:1 against 24.3% at 1:3.
